text:
aaron (Product): Customer-ACME pushed hard for private deploy + streaming + audit logs. They want GA-ish runway ~May 15. Need to lock scope and sequencing. Who owns the handoff for runtime changes vs infra reservations?

maya (Program Mgmt): Adding context from customer call — primary ask: steady token throughput (low p95 latency), full audit trail to KMS, and model fallback for capacity spikes. They said partial rollout is fine.

alex (Eng): Short answer: runtime needs a KV-prefix caching change + optional streaming path. That intersects with infra capacity and security hooks. Estimate: 2w runtime dev + 1w integration + canary.

sam (Runtime): Agree with alex. The KV change is compatible with existing models but needs a rolling restart of runtime nodes. I can do it but will need reserved pool during canary.

janet (Infra): Reserved pool is straightforward but we need exact sizing. If we assume 4 GPUs for steady and 2 for burst, we can schedule. Also need network egress specifics for private deploy.

liam (Security): Audit logs: we need an event stream to ship to customer KMS/HSM and an export that meets SOC + our internal retention. That will touch the control plane and agent. Expect ~5d spec + 5d work.

nora (SRE): Operationally, add a canary window and an automated rollback on error rate + latency spike. Also want a traffic shadow to check audit export correctness before flipping.

aaron (Product): Ok — can we map dependencies and a minimal launch surface? My proposal for MVP (must-haves): 1) private deploy toggle, 2) streaming responses (server-sent events), 3) audit export (event stream + KMS encryption), 4) model fallback policy. Optional: advanced batching tweaks.

alex (Eng): Proposed sequencing: Phase A (runtime + security spec), Phase B (infra provisioning + private control-plane wiring), Phase C (canary + customer test). If any single item slips, we can ship streaming + fallback earlier and gate audit export.

sam (Runtime): Phase A tasks I own: - KV prefix change (3d dev) - streaming path (4d dev) - integration tests (3d) Will need 2 GPUs reserved for dev cluster and 4 GPUs for canary.

janet (Infra): Phase B tasks: - reserve dedicated pool: estimate 6xA100 equivalent for 99th percentile load - setup VPC peering & private control plane - add plumbing for audit export (forwarder)

liam (Security): Phase A tasks: - spec audit events (schema + retention) - KMS integration checklist - threat model update. Need a security review slot; prefer a 3-day review window.

nora (SRE): Phase C: define canary metrics: p95 latency, error-rate, audit export delivery success. Canary policy: 10% traffic for 2 hours -> 50% -> 100% if green. Rollback on 2x baseline error or >25% p95 increase.

aaron (Product): Can we put concrete dates? Customer asked for May 15. Today is planning day here and we should be realistic. If we start next Monday: A = 2w, B = 1w, C = 1w. That hits May 15 only if nothing slips. Thoughts?

alex (Eng): Tight but possible if we parallelize security spec with runtime dev. I can reassign one senior to help sam to shave a few days.

liam (Security): We can start spec now in parallel, but KMS/HSM procurement and contract changes with customer might add lead time. Put a blocker on any GA date until contract confirms KMS endpoint.

janet (Infra): I'll queue the capacity request now but will mark it conditional on final sizing. If customer confirms load profile this week we'll lock slots.

maya (Program Mgmt): I'll push for the customer to provide production RPS and token distribution by EOD tomorrow. Also will surface the KMS requirement to their infra lead.

nora (SRE): Quick ask — instrument the canary to emit the following trace tags: `env`, `model_variant`, `route`, `audit_ok` so we can filter failures.

sam (Runtime): noted. I'll add those trace tags in the runtime and include a small test harness.

aaron (Product): Backup plan if audit export misses GA: ship streaming + private toggle + fallback; mark audit export as P1 for post-GA (2w after). Is that acceptable to customer?

maya (Program Mgmt): I'll confirm. They said audit logs are very important, but they allowed phased rollouts previously. I'll confirm tradeoff today.

alex (Eng): Also flag: if we decouple audit export, security still needs the schema early or we'll have rework. So draft schema before GA regardless.

liam (Security): Agreed. We'll deliver schema by end of week.

janet (Infra): I'll start a provisional reservation and label it `customer-acme-mvp`. CLI for reserving we used before:```
redwood dedicate reserve --pool=customer-acme-mvp --gpus=6 --start=2024-05-08 --duration=30d
```

nora (SRE): Canary policy snippet for ops handbook:```
canary:
  steps:
    - percent: 10
      duration: 2h
    - percent: 50
      duration: 4h
    - percent: 100
      duration: 24h
rollback_criteria:
  - error_rate > 2x_baseline
  - p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.25
  - audit_delivery_failures > 0.5%\n```

deploy-bot: calendar event created: "ACME private deploy SOC run" May 10 09:00 - 10:00 (organizer: maya)

aaron (Product): Action items recap: 1) sam/alex: runtime deliverables & dev cluster sizing (due in 3d) 2) liam: schema + security review slot (due in 5d) 3) janet: provisional reserve + network checklist (due in 2d) 4) maya: confirm customer RPS + KMS endpoint (due EOD tomorrow) 5) nora: ops canary doc (due in 4d)

maya (Program Mgmt): I'll update the roadmap board and tag owners. Will ping again after customer confirmation. :thumbsup:

alex (Eng): I'll post a short tech note in #eng-runtime with the KV change and streaming outline.

sam (Runtime): starting work tomorrow, will post progress daily in this thread.

liam (Security): I'll schedule the review and post calendar invite.

nora (SRE): I'll prep runbooks for rollback and observability dashboards.

janet (Infra): reserving provisional pool now.

aaron (Product): Thanks all. If anything blocks schedule, flag here immediately.

maya (Program Mgmt): tagging @alex @sam @liam @janet @nora for visibility.
